notice: RN bank batch 137: Maternity case studies: first prenatal visit, fetal growth restriction, ruptured ectopic pregnancy and second-line uterotonics. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate the type of sign of pregnancy.

rationale.correct: Only signs produced by the fetus are positive signs.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.stem: Using the history, choose the correct values.

rationale.correct: GTPAL: G4 T1 P1 A1 L3.

perOption.b1:a: Son, twins (one pregnancy), miscarriage, and now.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

exhibits.title: History
exhibits.body: Son at 39 weeks; twins at 34 weeks, both living; miscarriage at 8 weeks.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: Using the Naegele rule, the estimated due date is {{b1}}, and the most important change to make now is {{b2}}.

rationale.correct: Add 7 days, subtract 3 months; smoking is the key risk.

perOption.b1:a: March 10 + 7 days = March 17, minus 3 months = December 17.
perOption.b2:a: Linked to growth restriction, abruption and SIDS.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.stem: Which parts of the first-visit plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Avoid all caffeine completely for the whole pregnancy
Raw sushi and unpasteurized soft cheese are fine to eat

rationale.correct: Vitamins, smoking cessation, routine labs and IPV screening.

perOption.e: Up to 200 mg a day is acceptable.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

options.text: Fewer fetal movements later in pregnancy
Mild ankle swelling at the end of the day

rationale.correct: Bleeding, headache, fluid and reduced movement are danger signs.

questions.stem: After surgery, the client cries and says, "I lost my baby and maybe my chance to have more." Which responses are therapeutic? Select all that apply.

options.text: "You've had a real loss. I'm here with you."
"Would you like me to call someone to be with you?"
"Many conceive with one tube; let's ask your doctor."
"At least it was early, before you got too attached."
"You can always try again soon, and next time will be fine."

rationale.correct: Acknowledge the loss and give support and accurate information.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

caseStudies.title: First prenatal visit with pregnancy terminology

exhibits.title: First prenatal visit
exhibits.body: A 29-year-old client comes for a first prenatal visit. The first day of the last menstrual period was March 10. The client has had a son born at 39 weeks, twins born at 34 weeks (both living), and one miscarriage at 8 weeks. The client smokes 5 cigarettes a day and takes no vitamins.

caseStudies.title: Fetal growth restriction found by fundal height

exhibits.title: 32 weeks
exhibits.body: A 34-year-old client at 32 weeks by early ultrasound has chronic hypertension and smokes. The client says the baby moves less than before.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 26-year-old client with a history of pelvic inflammatory disease has had spotting and right lower abdominal pain for 2 days. The last period was 7 weeks ago. Today the pain became sudden and severe, and the client has right shoulder pain and fainted at home.

rows.label: Ultrasound
cells: Empty uterus; free fluid in the pelvis

exhibits.title: 15 minutes after a vaginal birth
exhibits.body: A 37-year-old client (G5 P5) with asthma and chronic hypertension had a long labor with oxytocin augmentation and a 4,300 g baby. Oxytocin 40 units in 1 L is running and fundal massage was done, but bleeding continues.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
